key_insight: Raising cold-spray pressure from 30 to 60 bar increased particle velocity above the critical deposition threshold for copper, producing denser, better-bonded deposits with higher ductility and conductivity.
engineering_relevance: For copper CSAM, spray pressure is a primary process lever for balancing mechanical integrity and electrical performance without melting the material.
method: Cold-sprayed copper at 30, 40, 50, and 60 bar using a LightSPEE3D system
Characterised deposits by XRD, SEM, hardness, eddy current conductivity, and tensile testing
Compared microstructure, particle bonding, and property trends versus spray pressure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pressure-dependent XRD refinement, increased conductivity, reduced hardness, and a clear tensile strength-to-ductility transition toward fully ductile fracture at higher pressures.
watch_item: Higher pressure improved performance, but the apparent recovery/recrystallisation that lowers hardness suggests the optimum window must be tuned to the target strength-conductivity tradeoff.
paper_title: Optimising Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing: Pressure-driven enhancement of mechanical performance in copper deposits
